english.title: Use Royal Arms without authorisation
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without the authority of His Majesty, used in connection with a business, namely **(..SPECIFY BUSINESS..), the Royal arms or arms so closely resembling the Royal arms as to be calculated to deceive in such manner as to be calculated to lead to the belief that you were duly authorised to use the Royal arms
english.legislation: Contrary to section 99(1) and (3) of the Trade Marks Act 1994.

english.notes: (i) Contravention of section 99(1) of the Trades Marks Act 1994 may be restrained by injunction proceedings - see section 99(4).(ii) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.
